headline: EU and UK urge Iran to halt Hormuz attacks and hybrid operations in Europe
body:
What happened: The European Union and Britain issued a joint statement after a Brussels summit condemning Iranian attacks on neighbouring states and on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. They demanded Tehran end its destabilising activity and what they called hybrid attacks on European soil, and reaffirmed that Iran must never obtain a nuclear weapon. Leaders also signed a pledge rejecting any tolls or fees for passage through the strait and agreed closer cooperation against cyber and hybrid threats.

The statement follows Iran-linked incidents in Europe, including a French probe into a cyber attack on supermarket refrigeration systems and convictions in Britain for spying on Iran International journalists. A US official separately told the Jerusalem Post that Iran has increasingly used anti-ship cruise missiles against vessels, while oil traffic through the strait remained high.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Reuters, Arab News, Asharq Al-Awsat, Jerusalem Post.

headline: Houthi missile debris reportedly damages Riyadh financial district tower
body:
What happened: Saudi Arabia's Houthi conflict widened on Thursday as the Saudi-led coalition said it had dealt with a missile launched by Yemen's Houthi movement towards Riyadh. Debris fell and caused material damage, though the extent was still being assessed. Reports said the Public Investment Fund tower in the capital's King Abdullah Financial District was hit, and casualties were not immediately known.

Earlier, Saudi civil defence authorities lifted threat alerts for the southern cities of Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait, after the Houthis claimed missile and drone attacks on sites there. The attacks follow the group's recent advances on Yemen's Red Sea coast.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Reuters, AP, Arab News, SCMP.

headline: Ukraine's NATO bid revived as allies meet in Berlin
body:
What happened: Ukraine's NATO membership is back on the agenda after a Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin, co-hosted by France, Germany and the UK, with President Zelenskyy attending. French President Macron urged allies to speed up delivery of air defence systems and to reopen the question of Ukraine's accession, citing Russia's maximalist position. Zelenskyy said membership would offer the clearest guarantees, but that it is too early to decide, as everything depends on how and when the war ends.

The discussions came hours after a trilateral summit in China between Trump, Putin and Xi, and reports say the US is open to a guarantee similar to NATO's mutual defence clause. Zelenskyy said a real guarantee would mean US or European forces and bases on Ukrainian soil. Germany expects new peace talks soon, possibly in the UAE.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Reuters, France 24, Euronews.

headline: US Central Command rejects Iranian claim of striking F-16 over Gulf
body:
What happened: US Central Command has rejected an Iranian claim that its air defences fired a missile at a US F-16 over the Gulf, damaging the jet and forcing an emergency landing. Iranian state media had reported the strike on Friday evening, saying the aircraft aborted its mission and landed at a nearby airport. CENTCOM said Iran did not attack an F-16 at all and that all US fighter jets in the region were safe and accounted for.

Iran has made similar claims during the conflict about shooting down or damaging US aircraft, and Washington has denied each one. The wider war began in February when the United States and Israel attacked Iran and has since spread across the Middle East, killing thousands and disrupting shipping and energy prices.

Reported by: Arab News. Also covered by Asharq Al-Awsat, Xinhua, China Daily.

headline: World court set to rule on Rohingya genocide claims against Myanmar
body:
What happened: The International Court of Justice in The Hague will deliver its judgment on Thursday in The Gambia's case accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority. The Gambia says Myanmar's 2017 military offensive in Rakhine State was meant to destroy the group, which drove at least 730,000 people into Bangladesh. Myanmar denies genocidal intent, calling its operations a counterinsurgency response. The ruling is final and cannot be appealed, though the court has limited means to enforce it, and it could be the first time the court finds a state guilty of genocide.

Reported by: Arab News. Also covered by AP, Le Monde, The Irrawaddy.

headline: Ukraine says Crimean Bridge is a legitimate target after strikes; Putin rules out talks
body:
What happened: Ukrainian forces struck the Crimean Bridge, linking occupied Crimea to Russia, on the night of November 17, 2026, damaging a section of its roadway. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the bridge is a legitimate target because Russia occupied Crimea, built the crossing and treats it as Russian territory, and that it will not stand during or after the war. He argued Russia uses it to move military equipment. Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would no longer discuss ceasefires covering energy infrastructure and Black Sea shipping, and vowed retaliation.

Reports say Ukraine used Ruta missiles made by a Dutch firm, Destinus, which confirmed its weapons were used. Days later a Russian drone crashed near the Dutch Embassy in Kyiv, slightly damaging the building.

Reported by: Kyiv Independent. Also covered by Reuters, BBC News, Meduza, The Moscow Times.

headline: Tehran's top diplomat says Beijing and Moscow back Iran's nuclear doctrine
body:
What happened: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said China and Russia oppose changing Tehran's nuclear doctrine, in an interview published Saturday by the state-run Iran Daily. He described the question as serious and divisive at home, with supporters and opponents of a shift. Some hardliners argue a change could open the way to a nuclear weapon as a deterrent. Araghchi said the official position has not changed. Iran has restricted the IAEA from inspecting its nuclear sites, and the UN watchdog recently urged incremental steps to restore access. Mojtaba Khamenei, who succeeded his father after a February US-Israeli strike, has not issued a decree altering the fatwa.

Reported by: The New Arab. Also covered by Arab News, The Hindu.

headline: Israeli strikes on Hamas commanders continue as Gaza deaths and arms financing draw scrutiny
body:
What happened: The Israeli military says its Southern Command has carried out a series of targeted strikes on Hamas brigade commanders in Gaza, aiming to stop the group rebuilding its capabilities. An IDF officer rejected accusations of deliberately harming civilians and said Hamas exploits civilians and hospitals. Separately, medical sources cited by Reuters and Al Jazeera reported at least four Palestinians killed by Israeli fire in one day, including a six-year-old boy in Deir el-Balah. A Dawn investigation also reported that Deutsche Bank backed a deal financing gearbox parts for Israel's Merkava tanks, which have been used in incidents that killed civilians.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Al Jazeera, Middle East Eye, Arab News, The New Arab.

headline: Putin rejects energy and sea truce after Ukraine hits Crimea bridge
body:
What happened: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow will retaliate for Ukrainian strikes on the bridge linking Russia to Crimea, and that he is dropping any idea of a mutual moratorium on attacks on energy facilities and shipping. Speaking in Shenzhen after meetings with the Chinese and U.S. leaders, he said he had asked his Security Council to consider a possible halt to attacks at sea and on energy sites. The comments followed the third Ukrainian strike on the bridge in a week, which briefly suspended train services. Separately, Ukraine's General Staff said it hit a Russian ammunition depot in occupied Crimea, two command posts in Zaporizhzhia and Donetsk, and a road bridge near Luhansk, while Crimea faces widespread power outages.

Reported by: Xinhua. Also covered by Reuters, Japan Times, SCMP, Meduza.

headline: Russian missile strikes hit Kyiv bridges and power, killing eight across Ukraine
body:
What happened: Russia launched a large overnight barrage on Ukraine, with Kyiv's Dnipro River bridges and power infrastructure among the targets. Ukrainian officials said eight people were killed, including six in Kyiv and two in Lviv, and dozens were wounded. Moscow framed the attack as retaliation for Ukraine's strikes on the Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia with Crimea, and Russia's Defence Ministry said it targeted bridges used to move military equipment.

Poland said three objects, likely two missiles and a drone, entered its airspace during the attack, which Warsaw called a Russian provocation. The strikes came as US-led ceasefire mediation made little visible progress.

Reported by: AP. Also covered by Al Jazeera, DW, France 24, Le Monde.

headline: Denmark expels Russian defence attaché over alleged plot against Ukrainian rapper
body:
What happened: Denmark is expelling Russia's defence attaché after prosecutors and intelligence services linked a failed plot to kill a Ukrainian-American rapper in Copenhagen to Russian intelligence. Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said the attaché must leave within seven days. Two Danish men, reportedly tied to the criminal gang Loyal to Familia, have been charged and held in custody; both have reportedly pleaded not guilty. The rapper, Kyivstoner, had cancelled a Danish concert after being warned of a threat to his life.

Denmark's intelligence service says the plot was planned and initiated by Russian services. Police have also announced a nationwide crackdown on the gang. Moscow's response was not reported in the coverage provided.

Reported by: France 24. Also covered by Euronews, Kyiv Independent, Xinhua.

headline: EU and UK set to advance post-Brexit deals at Brussels summit
body:
What happened: The UK and European Union are holding a summit in Brussels to set the long-term shape of their relationship after Brexit. Prime Minister Andy Burnham, European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen and European Council president António Costa are attending; the meeting was delayed from July after Keir Starmer resigned. Three agreements are expected: easing trade in meat, cheese, wine and flowers, linking emissions trading systems, and a youth mobility scheme for 18- to 30-year-olds. Tuition fees and visa numbers remain unresolved, and the EU is tying all three deals together.

The UK has not been included in the EU's Made in Europe industrial plan, as that law is not expected to be finalised until spring 2027, with France and the European Parliament taking a stricter line.

Reported by: The Guardian. Also covered by Reuters, AP, BBC News, Al Jazeera.

headline: Tanker attacks in Hormuz raise pollution fears and push oil prices
body:
What happened: Attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have intensified, with reports of several vessels exploding after striking naval mines and at least two seafarers missing. Endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh entered the waters during the blasts to highlight the environmental toll, warning that oil contamination could take decades to clean up after the fighting ends. Brent crude nonetheless edged up on Thursday, trading near $92.58 a barrel, though it had fallen sharply earlier in the month as Middle East exports neared prewar levels. Iran is widely linked to the strikes in the reporting, though attribution could not be independently verified.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Reuters, Middle East Eye, Japan Times, Arab News.

headline: US reinforces Gulf naval presence as Iran standoff drags on
body:
What happened: A third US aircraft carrier group, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, has arrived in the Middle East, adding to Washington's forces around Iran. The US says it prefers economic pressure, including a naval blockade of Iranian ports and a land blockade called Task Force Iron Gate, over renewed large-scale strikes. Reports say US sailors face longer deployments and shortages of fresh food.

Iran and the US have been trading limited attacks while both keep blockades around the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts say the stalemate could last for months but carries growing economic costs, especially for Iran. Iran's leadership has rejected a state of "neither war nor peace," and oil prices remain about 30 percent above pre-war levels.

Reported by: Asharq Al-Awsat. Also covered by Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera, The Guardian.

headline: Russian missiles and drone fall in Poland during massive strike on Ukraine
body:
What happened: During a large overnight Russian attack on Ukraine on November 20, two missiles and a jet-powered drone came down on Polish territory in the southeast, Poland's defence minister said. One missile is believed to have landed about 50km from the Ukrainian border, close to where European troops were holding a military exercise. No injuries or damage were reported. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the incident an apparent intentional provocation by Moscow, while analysts see it as part of a wider pattern of Russian incursions testing NATO's response.

The episode came as Ukraine faced one of the heaviest bombardments of the war, with Kyiv's bridges and railway stations also hit, and as US envoys pushed new peace talks that Moscow rejected on Ukraine's NATO-style guarantees.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by AP, BBC News, The Guardian, France 24.

headline: China, Russia and US leaders issue joint declaration after Shenzhen summit
body:
What happened: Leaders of China, Russia and the United States met in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026, for a first trilateral summit and then released a joint declaration toward peace. The three presidents said they were committed to strategic stability and international security. Their statement pledged to reform the United Nations, which the three permanent Security Council members said should respond more effectively to global challenges.

The declaration also said the three countries would expand production and supply of refined petroleum products and stressed the importance of stable energy flows. It added that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and announced a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation.

Reported by: China Daily. Also covered by Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera, The Guardian.

headline: Moscow rejects quasi-NATO guarantees for Ukraine as US floats Article 5-style protection
body:
What happened: US envoy Jared Kushner said Washington is open to security guarantees for post-war Ukraine modelled on NATO's Article 5 mutual defence clause, and claimed Russia is comfortable with the idea. He spoke at a meeting in Berlin of around 40 European allies of Ukraine, days after a first-ever summit in China involving Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Kushner said any guarantee would need to serve American interests and form part of a wider security package.

Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov rejected any form of quasi-membership of NATO for Kyiv, while French President Emmanuel Macron called for Ukraine's NATO membership to be reconsidered. The claim about Russia's comfort could not be independently verified.

Reported by: AP. Also covered by Reuters, Al Jazeera, NPR, Le Monde.

headline: Overnight Russian strikes hit Kyiv bridges and kill several across Ukraine
body:
What happened: Russia carried out a large overnight air attack on Ukraine, with missiles and drones striking Kyiv and other regions. Kyiv's mayor said three bridges over the Dnipro River were damaged, disrupting traffic in the capital, and citywide power outages were reported. Ukrainian officials put the death toll at eight, including six in Kyiv, with dozens wounded. The attack followed a Ukrainian strike on the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea, which Moscow's leader Vladimir Putin vowed to answer.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia launched more than 400 drones and over 110 missiles, targeting civilian energy and transport infrastructure. Russia's defence ministry said it hit military-industrial sites and bridges used to move weapons. Diplomatic efforts toward a ceasefire showed little progress, with Moscow rejecting any form of Ukrainian NATO membership.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by AP, Al Jazeera, The Guardian, France 24.

headline: Somalia orders UAE envoy out and recalls its own ambassador from Abu Dhabi
body:
What happened: Somalia has told the United Arab Emirati ambassador to leave within 72 hours and has pulled its own envoy back from Abu Dhabi. Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud announced the move at a news conference in Mogadishu, describing an "open invasion" against Somalia's sovereignty and unity and warning of measures against anyone cooperating with the UAE. The UAE foreign ministry did not immediately respond, while a senior Emirati adviser condemned the remarks.

The move follows accusations from President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud that the UAE has built military bases outside national security structures, funded armed groups and opponents of the central government, and interfered in internal affairs. Ties have been strained for years over the UAE's support for Somaliland, and worsened in January when Somalia annulled agreements with the UAE on ports, security and defence.

Reported by: Premium Times. Also covered by Middle East Eye, Xinhua.

headline: Iran claims it downed another US MQ-9 drone over Hormuz
body:
What happened: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps said its aerospace forces shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of Saturday, using a newly deployed air defence system. The IRGC described it as the 58th MQ-9 downed by Iranian forces. Iranian officials said they monitor military and aerial activity in the strategic waterway and will respond firmly to violations of their airspace. The claim could not be independently verified. The MQ-9 Reaper is a medium-altitude drone used by the US military for surveillance and strikes. The report places the incident within the wider US-Israeli conflict with Iran that began in late February.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Middle East Eye, Fars, Mehr News.

headline: Trump's Asia trip ends without a Kim meeting as Pyongyang stays silent
body:
What happened: US President Donald Trump repeatedly sought a meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his Asia tour this week, but Kim did not respond and no encounter took place. Kim was instead shown in state media visiting a ski resort, a sacred mountain and a naval university. Trump left Asia after a trilateral summit with the leaders of China and Russia, saying he was too busy and that a meeting would happen at some point.

Analysts doubt that real contacts preceded the offer. They note that Pyongyang is unlikely to engage unless Washington moves toward recognising it as a nuclear state, while the US still demands denuclearisation. North Korea's growing support from Russia and China reduces its need to talk with Washington, though experts say a future meeting remains possible.

Reported by: SCMP. Also covered by Arab News, CNA, Dawn.

headline: California subpoenas Nvidia over possible chip diversion to China and investor disclosures
body:
What happened: California's attorney general, Rob Bonta, has issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia, examining whether its advanced semiconductor chips reached China despite US export restrictions and whether the company misled investors. The probe follows the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang after reports of multiple affairs, including one with a woman linked to Singapore-based Megaspeed, which has bought nearly $5bn of Nvidia hardware and is being examined over possible chip diversion to China. Megaspeed says it operates legally. Nvidia's shares have fallen about a fifth since Huang's admission, and Huang is due to testify before congressional committees on 1 December.

Reported by: AP. Also covered by The Guardian.

headline: Israeli tank raid in central Gaza ends; Palestinian militias accused of support
body:
What happened: Israel's military said it had completed a ground operation in central Gaza that began Wednesday, targeting what it described as a tunnel crossing beneath the Yellow Line. The incursion, the first major Israeli ground move beyond the line since the October 2025 ceasefire, prompted roughly 6,000 Palestinians to flee, according to Gaza's government media office. Residents returned Thursday to find the Salah al-Din road scarred by track marks and earthen barriers, and at least one person was reported killed in nearby strikes.

Palestinian sources and analysts alleged that Israeli-backed local armed groups took part in the operation, intimidating families into leaving their homes. These claims could not be independently verified, and Hamas called the raid a blatant ceasefire violation.

headline: Ukraine's European allies gather in Berlin as US envoys join talks
body:
What happened: Leaders of the Coalition of the Willing, a group of countries backing Ukraine, met in Berlin on November 19 to show a united front and press for a European role in any peace talks. The gathering came shortly after a three-way meeting in Shenzhen, China, between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe must be involved in any negotiations, while Kushner said Russia had grown comfortable with NATO Article 5-style guarantees for Ukraine, though Moscow has not commented.

Putin separately vowed retaliation after Ukrainian aerial attacks damaged the Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia, and proposed that European officials travel to Moscow. Ukrainian President Zelensky urged pressure on Russia and new European sanctions.

headline: Iraq deploys forces to militia town of Jurf al-Sakhar under negotiated arrangement
body:
What happened: Iraqi security forces moved into Jurf al-Sakhar, a town south of Baghdad long controlled by the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah militia, on Friday, state media said. The move follows a compromise brokered by senior Shi'ite politicians after Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered preparations to act against the group over alleged smuggling of hundreds of millions of dollars in state oil. Under the arrangement, Kataib fighters were expected to relocate to other areas, and nine officials have been dismissed in the probe. Kataib has denied the smuggling accusations.

Iran's Quds Force commander reportedly travelled to Baghdad to help ease tensions, and the group's leadership described the talks as positive. The operation tests Baghdad's wider push to disarm militias that have attacked US targets since the US and Israel struck Iran in February.

headline: Russian strikes hit Kyiv bridges and kill three, mayor says
body:
What happened: Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv killed three people and wounded about 15, city officials said on Friday. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said several bridges over the Dnipro River were hit, including the Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi and Pivdennyi crossings, causing closures and traffic limits affecting millions of commuters. The strikes also started fires and damaged infrastructure and buildings. Russia's Defence Ministry said it hit defence industry, energy and transport targets, and the attacks followed Vladimir Putin's vow of a painful response after Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge. Reuters could not immediately verify the reports.

Reported by: AP. Also covered by Reuters, France 24, Asharq Al-Awsat, Meduza.
